pages.summary:
This page presents data on prepaid Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) in Indonesia from 2008 to 2012, analyzing the factors behind its decline. It features two visual elements: Exhibit 1, a line chart showing the national average ARPU decreasing from Rp 38,000 in 2008 to Rp 30,000 in 2012, and Exhibit 2, a bar chart comparing ARPU across four major operators (Indosat, Telkomsel, XL, Smartfren) for the same years. The text explains that the initial drop was due to a government-initiated price war, which forced CDMA operators to lower tariffs, and that the continued decline is driven by reduced usage of SMS and voice calls as users shift to data-based services like IM and VoIP. The source is identified as Venture Consulting Analysis.

**Text Evidence:**
- Initially reduced ARPU was due to massive price war, initiated by the government.
- CDMA operators managed to force GSM operators to reduce their tariffs.
- Recently people use data-based IM, VoIP, etc., thus leads to even less usage of SMS and voice call.
- Tariffs have hit rock-bottom thus there will not be any price war anymore.
- Less usage on SMS and voice also lead to reduced ARPU.
- ARPU seems to be declining because of multi-sim usage and availability of cheap mobile phones.

**Visual Evidence:**
<figure_summary>Exhibit 1: Indonesia Prepaid ARPU (Rp'000) - Line chart showing the national average prepaid ARPU in Indonesia decreased from Rp 38,000 in 2008 to Rp 30,000 in 2012.</figure_summary>
<figure_summary>Exhibit 2: Prepaid ARPU (Rp'000) - Bar chart comparing the prepaid ARPU for four operators (Indosat, Telkomsel, XL, Smartfren) in 2008 and 2012, showing a general downward trend for all.</figure_summary>

This page presents Exhibit 3, a line chart forecasting the Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) in Indonesia from 2013 to 2017, broken down by voice, SMS, and mobile data services. The chart shows that Voice ARPU is expected to flatten, SMS ARPU will continue to decline, and Mobile Data ARPU will initially fall but then increase as data consumption grows. Key textual points explain these trends, noting that the overall declining ARPU trend will persist until 2015 when data users begin enrolling in larger plans, which will help compensate for losses in voice and SMS revenue.

- Voice ARPU will continue to flatten in the medium term.
- SMS ARPU will continue to decrease because the majority of users will be on smartphones eventually.
- Data ARPU will fall in the short term but will pick up later as users' data consumption increases.
- There is a continued trend of declining ARPU until 2015, after which data users will start to enroll for bigger data plans due to increased mobile internet usage, compensating for declining voice and SMS ARPU.

This page, titled "Internet Content Regulations," outlines key aspects of internet governance and content control. It details the passage of the UU ITE law by legislators to protect against malicious online activities like DoS attacks and hacking, noting that violations can lead to jail time. The Ministry of ICT's TrustPositif initiative is described as a method for blocking illegal sites such as those containing porn or gambling, with examples including Vimeo, Imgur, and Reddit being blocked. The text also explains that TrustPositif operates by blocking DNS requests, which can be circumvented using tools like UC Browser. A notable case involving politician Misbakhun is cited, where a Twitter user who accused him of corruption was jailed but later had the conviction overturned.

**Text Evidence:**
- Legislators passed UU ITE to protect people and businesses from malicious Internet activities (e.g., DoS, hacking, sniffing).
- Criminal acts over the Internet can result in prosecution and jail time if convicted.
- The Ministry of ICT deployed the TrustPositif initiative to block illegal sites (porn, gambling, etc.).
- Sites like Vimeo, Imgur, and Reddit are blocked due to allowing nudity videos.
- TrustPositif blocks DNS requests, which can be circumvented via UC Browser.
- Internet users can face libel suits or criminal prosecution for comments; a case involving politician Misbakhun is mentioned.

This slide, titled "Mobile Entertainment (1)", discusses the decline of the traditional music industry in Indonesia due to the shift from physical media like cassettes and CDs to digital formats such as MP3s on phones. It highlights the negative impact of this transition, including the closure of long-standing music stores by Aquarius and downsizing by Disc Tarra, which owns the largest physical music distribution chain. The slide also notes that local music apps like Telkom's MelOn, Telkomsel's Langitmusik, and GenID's MusikLegal have struggled to create profitable businesses despite being official digital repositories. A key financial figure cited is Smartfren's claim that the Indonesian digital music industry was worth $60 million for the last 12 months of 2014.

**Text Evidence:**
- Music industry sales of cassettes/CDs deteriorated due to increasing adoption of MP3s in phones.
- The Black October incident in Indonesia caused the music industry to become relatively quiet.
- Aquarius, one of the oldest music labels, closed its long-standing music stores in Jakarta.
- Disc Tarra, owner of the largest physical music distribution chain, downsized its shopping mall shops.
- Local music apps (MelOn, Langitmusik, MusikLegal) failed to bring profitable business.
- Smartfren claims the Indonesian digital music industry was worth $60 million for the last 12 months of 2014.

pages.ocr_text:
Table: How do users pay for mobile ecommerce in Indonesia?
| PSP Service | Description info:
| Coda Payments | Coda Payments is one of the earlier PSP that provides carrier billing with AXIS. Indonesia is a predominantly prepaid market, carrier billing can be considered as airtime/balance deduction. AXIS users can easily key in their AXIS mobile phone no into at merchants cooperating with Coda and it will send an SMS asking to confirm. Upon confirmation, the user's airtime balance will be deducted and payment is completed.
| Mimopay | Mimopay is the pioneer of accepting 3rdparty payments using telco's prepaid card (Smartfren's). Mimopay works with XL and Telkomsel for carrier billing. Similar to Coda, Mimopay also require users to key in their mobile phone no to confirm via SMS. For Smartfren prepaid reload cards, users can just key in the secret code into the merchants' website to claim the credits. Mimopay is the first PSP in Indonesia that deploys its own Android SDK to assist apps merchants in adopting Mimopay's various channels.
| Mandiri e-cash | Mandiri e-cash is the latest product of Mandiri, the largest bank in Indonesia. Mandiri e-cash has UMB/USSD access menu on every telco (*141*6#) or an app for Android/iOS users. Mandiri e-cash enables people with no bank account to easily own a Mandiri e-cash account by using their mobile phone no as their account no. This is a common product for banks to have because of the huge amount of unbanked people in Indonesia.
| BCA Klikpay | BCA Klikpay is BCA's answer to PayPal. BCA is the largest consumer bank in Indonesia, it has the largest no of ATMs and EDCs in the country. BCA Klikpay allows users to deduct their bank account balance directly. Most people own a BCA account in major cities across Indonesia, so this is a very convenient payment method.
| Doku/Veritrans/E2Pay/Indopay/Finpay/IPayMu/IPay88 | Doku and IPayMu aim to be Indonesia's PayPal. While Veritrans, E2Pay, Indopay, Finpay, and IPay88 are credit cards payment processor. Doku has its own wallet and has the widest coverage of merchants. Major merchants utilize Doku Wallet and Doku as their credit cards payment processor.

This page provides a detailed overview of mobile internet payment options in Indonesia, focusing on various Payment Service Providers (PSPs) and their methods. It describes five main PSP services: Coda Payments, Mimopay, Mandiri e-cash, BCA Klikpay, and a group of processors including Doku, Veritrans, E2Pay, Indopay, Finpay, IPayMu, and IPay88. The content explains how each service works, highlighting features like carrier billing, prepaid card usage, bank account integration, and wallet systems. The information is presented in a structured table format that compares the services based on their functionality and market reach.

**Text Evidence:**
- Coda Payments offers carrier billing with AXIS, allowing users to deduct airtime balance via SMS confirmation.
- Mimopay pioneers 3rd party payments using telco prepaid cards (Smartfren's) and works with XL and Telkomsel for carrier billing.
- Mandiri e-cash enables unbanked people to create accounts using their mobile phone number as the account ID.
- BCA Klikpay allows direct deduction from BCA bank accounts, leveraging BCA's extensive ATM and EDC network.
- Doku and IPayMu aim to be Indonesia's PayPal, while other listed companies are credit card processors; Doku has the widest merchant coverage.

**Visual Evidence:**
<table_summary>Table: How do users pay for mobile ecommerce in Indonesia? - This table lists five PSP services (Coda Payments, Mimopay, Mandiri e-cash, BCA Klikpay, and a group of others) and provides a description of each service's functionality, target users, and key features.</table_summary>

elements.text:
Table: How do users pay for mobile ecommerce in Indonesia?
| PSP Service | Description info:
| Coda Payments | Coda Payments is one of the earlier PSP that provides carrier billing with AXIS. Indonesia is a predominantly prepaid market, carrier billing can be considered as airtime/balance deduction. AXIS users can easily key in their AXIS mobile phone no into at merchants cooperating with Coda and it will send an SMS asking to confirm. Upon confirmation, the user's airtime balance will be deducted and payment is completed.
| Mimopay | Mimopay is the pioneer of accepting 3rdparty payments using telco's prepaid card (Smartfren's). Mimopay works with XL and Telkomsel for carrier billing. Similar to Coda, Mimopay also require users to key in their mobile phone no to confirm via SMS. For Smartfren prepaid reload cards, users can just key in the secret code into the merchants' website to claim the credits. Mimopay is the first PSP in Indonesia that deploys its own Android SDK to assist apps merchants in adopting Mimopay's various channels.
| Mandiri e-cash | Mandiri e-cash is the latest product of Mandiri, the largest bank in Indonesia. Mandiri e-cash has UMB/USSD access menu on every telco (*141*6#) or an app for Android/iOS users. Mandiri e-cash enables people with no bank account to easily own a Mandiri e-cash account by using their mobile phone no as their account no. This is a common product for banks to have because of the huge amount of unbanked people in Indonesia.
| BCA Klikpay | BCA Klikpay is BCA's answer to PayPal. BCA is the largest consumer bank in Indonesia, it has the largest no of ATMs and EDCs in the country. BCA Klikpay allows users to deduct their bank account balance directly. Most people own a BCA account in major cities across Indonesia, so this is a very convenient payment method.
| Doku/Veritrans/E2Pay/Indopay/Finpay/IPayMu/IPay88 | Doku and IPayMu aim to be Indonesia's PayPal. While Veritrans, E2Pay, Indopay, Finpay, and IPay88 are credit cards payment processor. Doku has its own wallet and has the widest coverage of merchants. Major merchants utilize Doku Wallet and Doku as their credit cards payment processor.
